newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy sends reinforcements to Naples gang war.
newsitem.headline: Italy sends reinforcements to Naples gang war.

text.p: Italy decided on Monday to send 200 extra police to the southern city of Naples to help crack down on an outbreak of gangland killings, the interior ministry said.
Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano made the decision after a weekend in which five people were murdered in an upsurge of in-fighting between rival clans of the Camorra, the Naples mafia.
On Sunday a man was shot dead as he strolled down the street in broad daylight, bringing the death toll from the latest violence in the city and surroundings to 89 in six months.

The 100 extra police and 100 Carabinieri paramilitary police being sent to Naples and nearby Caserta are intended to give "more effective control of the territory...as well as an intensification of investigations into the most aggressive clans", the ministry said.
Last week Rome sent 500 troops to do guard duty in the area and let police concentrate on quelling the bloody clan warfare.
But the presence of the troops, expected to stay until the end of the year, has not yet brought peace. Nine people have been murdered since their arrival.
Antonio Rastrelli, President of the Campania region of which Naples is the capital, said much more was needed.

"Organised crime has always thrived in particular areas of the region, where the only solution is a massive intervention by the army, coordinated by a high authority that can oversee joint efforts by police and the military," he said.
He also said social initiatives were vital to spur the region's depressed economy, which helped crime to take hold.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Sunday Italy's war against organised crime could only be won by boosting the economy and providing employment. Naples has a jobless rate of almost 25 percent.
"If we think the fight against the mob is only a fight against crime, then we have lost from the start," he said.
"We can win only by giving people, young and old, the hope they have lost."
